question: Read every site of BiceLib's 2024-2025 hooks and byte patches off the bytes, against an untouched copy of the executable, so the records that cited only the DLL's own source carry a reading instead.

addresses.name: Hook_LeaderRankChange
addresses.comment: In CPromoteLeaderCommand::Execute, the new rank stored: `mov [edi+0x6C], eax; cmp [edi+0x68], ebx` (89 47 6C 39 5F 68, vanilla), EDI the leader and EAX the rank; the cmp's flags feed the jne after it. BiceLib's RankSpecificTraits stands here and replays both. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded at 0x1D7CC8..0x1D7CE8 from both the vanilla and the installed exe, identical; `mov [edi+0x6C], eax` follows `add/sub eax, [esi+0x68]` on the direction byte at +0x64. Wrong if EDI were not the leader - CLeader +0x6C is rank in CLeader.hpp, read live.
addresses.revises: source was BiceLib/bice.cpp alone; now the bytes, the registers, and the flags dependency

addresses.name: Hook_LeaderSaveTrait
addresses.comment: In CLeader::SaveContents' trait loop: `add ecx, 0x2C; lea edi, [esp+0xC]` (83 C1 2C 8D 7C 24 0C, vanilla), ECX the trait (`mov ecx, [ebx]` at 0x17FF03, a list node's data), turned into its name (CTrait +0x2C) for the call at 0x17FF0F. BiceLib's RankSpecificTraits hands a blank string here for a rank-specific trait. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x17FEF2..0x17FF20 in both files: the loop loads [edi+0x30] (the leader's trait list), `mov ecx,[ebx]; mov ebx,[ebx+8]` walks it. CTrait::Offsets::name is 0x2C in CTrait.hpp. Wrong if the loop walked something other than the traits.
addresses.revises: source was BiceLib/bice.cpp alone; now the bytes and where ECX comes from

addresses.name: Hook_LeaderListShowSkill
addresses.comment: In CLeaderAssignmentEntry's constructor, after the skill (leader +0x70) is turned into text in a stack buffer by the runtime call at 0x79A0C4 (value, buffer, 10): `mov esi, eax; mov ecx, esi; add esp, 0xC` (8B F0 8B CE 83 C4 0C, vanilla), EAX the buffer, which is then measured and copied into the row's string. **The leader is [ebp+0x14]**, the constructor's fourth argument, read by the game at 0x365666; BiceLib's first hook here read the game's esp+0xC instead, which by the stack arithmetic is the EDI the prologue saved - the caller's register. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Bytes and [ebp+0x14] confirmed: `mov edx,[ebp+0x14]; mov eax,[edx+0x70]` at 0x365666, and the record's signature puts leader fourth. The saved-EDI claim is inferred from the prologue (push ebp; three SEH dwords; sub esp,0xB8; push ebx/esi/edi) with every call before the site assumed balanced, plus the three _itoa arguments still on the stack.
addresses.revises: source was BiceLib/bice.cpp alone; now where the leader really is, and what the old hook read

addresses.name: Hook_LeaderListShowSkillSelected
addresses.comment: In CLeaderAssignmentPanel's constructor, the same seven bytes as Hook_LeaderListShowSkill (8B F0 8B CE 83 C4 0C, vanilla) for the selected leader's skill. The leader is [ebp+0xC]: the unit argument's slot, which LeaderPanel_StoreUnitLeader (0x367935) has overwritten with the unit's leader; the game reads it at 0x3679B2. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x367900..0x3679F0: `mov edx,[ebp+0xC]; mov eax,[edx+0x12C]` ... `mov [ebp+0xC], eax` at 0x367935, then `mov edx,[ebp+0xC]; mov eax,[edx+0x70]` at 0x3679B2. No prologue or int3 padding between the function's start 0x3671A0 and the site.

addresses.name: LeaderPanel_StoreUnitLeader
addresses.comment: `mov dword ptr [ebp+0xC], eax` in CLeaderAssignmentPanel's constructor: the unit's leader (CUnit +0x12C, loaded at 0x367925) stored over the constructor's own `unit` argument, which is the leader from here on - the selected leader's name and skill are read through it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 3.

addresses.name: Hook_UnitAttachmentLimit
addresses.comment: In CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate, the count against the limit: `cmp dword ptr [ebp+8], 5; pop edi` (83 7D 08 05 5F, vanilla), then `jl` to the yes. [ebp+8] is the count, kept in the subordinate argument's own slot once EBX holds it (cleared at 0x1B96FE); EBX is the unit to attach and **EDI the last subordinate counted** (`mov edi, [esi]` each pass). ECX is not: it is `this` for the virtual call each pass makes, so whatever that call leaves - BiceLib's first hook read it there. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded the function from 0x1B96B0 to 0x1B974F in both files: `mov edi,[esi]; mov edx,[edi]; mov eax,[edx+0x3C]; mov esi,[esi+8]; mov ecx,edi; call eax` at 0x1B9710. Wrong if the count were somewhere else - the only `inc` in the loop is `inc dword ptr [ebp+8]` at 0x1B972C.
addresses.revises: source was BiceLib/bice.cpp alone, and said ECX was the last counted unit; it is EDI

addresses.name: UnitAttachmentLimit_EarlyExit
addresses.comment: `test esi, esi; je 0x1B974B` in CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate, after `mov esi, [esi+0x1E4]` (the commander's first subordinate node): with no subordinates the function answers true here, before the counting loop and before it pushes EDI - so Hook_UnitAttachmentLimit is only reached with one counted. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x1B96F8..0x1B9710; 0x1B974B is `pop esi; mov al, 1`. CUnit::Offsets::children is 0x1E4. Was inferred from the DLL's comment.

addresses.name: Hook_NavyScreenPenalty
addresses.comment: In CNavalCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers, the test that starts the poor-screens penalty: `cmp esi, edx; jge 0x1665F6` (3B F2 0F 8D 8E 00 00 00, vanilla), ESI the screens, EDX the capital ships (already above 0, `jle` at 0x16655A), and [esp+0x1C] the penalty, set to EBX - zeroed at 0x1664E9 - at 0x166554. The sliding scale follows to 0x1665F2. BiceLib's NavyScreenPenalty replaces test and scale with a flat penalty below a ratio. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x166530..0x166610 in both files, and 0x166480..0x1664F0 for the `xor ebx, ebx`. Wrong if [esp+0x1C] were not the penalty - the scale's end stores its result there at 0x1665F2.

Nothing from here reads EDX or EAX before setting them - `mov edx, [esp+0x18]` at 0x166600 - as the scale's own end leaves both changed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.

addresses.name: Hook_OffmapIc_CountLocalIc
addresses.comment: In CCountry::UpdateIC's province loop: `mov ecx, [esi+0x330]` (8B 8E 30 03 00 00, vanilla), just after the province's term `IC * (1000 + LOCAL_IC) / 1000` is in EAX - the province modifier's values at [esi+0x114] (CMapProvince::modifier + CModifier::values), entries +0x78 (IC) and +0x80 (LOCAL_IC). ESI the province, EBX the country. The term is added to the sum whatever the owner test after it says (0xF0F6F). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xF0EB0..0xF0FA0 in both files. 0xFC + 0x18 = 0x114 and entry 15 * 8 = 0x78, 16 * 8 = 0x80 by CModifier.hpp. Wrong if the sum at [ebp+8] skipped some terms - `test eax,eax; jle; add [ebp+8], eax` is the only add.

addresses.name: Hook_OffmapIc_SetBaseIc
addresses.comment: In CCountry::UpdateIC, the total stored: `mov [ebx+0x604], eax` (89 83 04 06 00 00, vanilla) - total_ic - then +0x60C. EAX the provinces' sum in whole IC (divided by 1000 through 0x10624DD3 from 0xF0F8B); ECX [ebx+0xDA8], which is global_modifier (+0xD90) + CModifier::values (+0x18), the global modifier's value array. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 2.

addresses.name: Hook_PlaceBuildingCheck
addresses.comment: In CBuildingDeployment::CanDeployIn: `test al, al; je 0x17E5B7` (84 C0 0F 84 CA 00 00 00, vanilla) on CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed's answer, called at 0x17E4E0 with the building [edi+0x38]; EDI the deployment, EBX the province. 0x17E5B7 is the refusal, 0x17E4ED the way on. BiceLib's PlaceUnresearchedBuildings skips the answer and asks only whether the level already there is below max_allowed_level - which also skips IsBuildingAllowed's control, queued-levels, port, not_if_x_exists and prerequisite checks. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 7.

addresses.comment: **Gives a leader a trait.** The leader from [ebp+8], the trait from [ebp+0xC], nothing from ECX, both exits `ret 8` (0x181C2A, 0x181C44). Before anything is added it tests the byte at trait + leader type (+0x68) + 0x2B0 - three bytes on the trait, one per leader type. BiceLib's addTraitToLeader calls it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 8.

addresses.name: Patch_MinisterTechDecay
addresses.comment: In CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers, the third pass over tech_decay_modifier (+0x1174): `mov [ecx+esi], eax` (89 04 31, vanilla) stores technology_status (+0xDF8) -> +0x1F8 [category] over each category - after the rebuild zeroed them (0xDDFBA) and added every minister's figure (0xDE37B), so vanilla throws the ministers' figures away. BiceLib's fixMinisterTechDecay makes it `add` (01 04 31). **The installed exe already holds 01 here**, written on disk. Not the `decay` effect's handler, which FINDINGS-techdecay.md section 4 said. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, sections 1 and 4.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xDDF9E..0xDDFC4 and 0xDE36F..0xDE3F4; the function record puts 0xDDD80..0xDF97D around both. Vanilla byte 89 from the untouched copy.

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bicelibsites.md, section 4.

addresses.name: Patch_QueuedHistoricalModel
addresses.comment: **A BiceLib patch site.** `cmp eax, [esi+0x18]; jae 0x82FF1` (3B 46 18 73 CC, vanilla, then 8B F0 83 C0 0C 39 16) - in CBrigadeConstructionDefinition::LoadKey's `historical_model` arm, the end of the search through the model's 12-byte entries for one technology of the unit type; the `jae` is what skips a technology the model does not name, so the levels after it shift in the line's list. fixQueuedHistoricalModel writes a 5-byte `jmp` over the two instructions to a stub that repeats the test, goes on to 0x83025 if an entry is left, and otherwise points esi at a zeroed entry and jumps to the append at 0x8302E (8B 5F 04 6A 10), which reads the level from [esi+4] - so the technology gets level 0, what CHistoricalModel::ApplyTo gives it on the map. esi is free to change: the outer loop reloads it from [esp+0xc] at 0x8301C before every search and the function's exit at 0x82E25 pops it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildqueue.md, section 10.
